caption: Given a matrix, Median is column-wise
Unsorted data is sorted first; the middle pair 3 and 4 averages to $\frac{7}{2}$
Exact constants are ordered by value, putting $e$ in the middle
The median of a lazy [[Range]] of even length is the mean of the middle two
The median of a 30-digit numeric list is a float
Columnwise over a three-dimensional array of data
The same outlier-laden data as in [[Mean]]'s example: the median of 1 barely moves, unlike the mean's $-\frac{38}{3}$
Robust to the outlier $100000$, unlike the mean
For an odd-length list, the median is the middle element of the sorted list. See [[Sort]]
Even count: the average of the two middle values, $2$ and $3$
Stays an exact rational for exact data
